questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is an example of step growth polymerisation?
questions.solution: Nylon 6,6 is an example of step growth polymerisation. As monomers adipic acid and hexamethylenediamine are bifunctional and form bond with the loss of simple molecules. The dimer formed also contains two functional groups, thus undergoes a series of condensation reaction in a stepwise manner.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is an example of step growth polymerisation?
questions.solution:
Step growth polymerization, also known as condensation polymerization, involves the reaction of bifunctional or polyfunctional monomers with the elimination of small molecules like water, alcohol, or ammonia. In this process, the polymer chain grows by the reaction of any two species present in the mixture.

Nylon 6,6 is formed by the condensation reaction between hexamethylenediamine ($H_{2}N(CH_{2})_{6}NH_{2}$) and adipic acid ($HOOC(CH_{2})_{4}COOH$). This reaction proceeds with the elimination of water molecules, which is a characteristic feature of step growth polymerization.

In contrast, Buna-S, Neoprene, and Teflon are formed via chain growth polymerization (addition polymerization), where the reaction proceeds through the addition of monomer units to an active center (free radical or ionic) without the elimination of small molecules.

Answer: Nylon 6,6

questions.q: Which of the following will form a biodegradable polymer?
questions.solution: Glycine and aminocaproic acid forms nylon- 2 -nylon- 6 , which is a biodegradable polymer.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is an addition polymer?
questions.solution: Neoprene and teflon are formed by addition polymerisation, while terylene and nylon-6,6 are formed by condensation polymerisation.
